--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The probe says periodic defects on the first two positions of each five-round cycle. So round 1 is always D. So they will defect on round 1. So we catch them."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like conditional strategy with forgiveness; the trace simulates a new strategy that cooperates initially, switches to always-defect if the opponent defects on round 1, tests always-cooperative opponents with isolated defections, and otherwise uses TFT-like logic. The trace proposes adding an exploit mode against always-cooperative opponents and handling always-defect/periodic opponents via round-1 defection detection.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these measurements when deciding what to retain or change to maximize cumulative tournament fitness." (the trace treats the probe measurements as the fitness target and designs the exploit around them)
STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional/forgiving strategy (slot 10-like) that defects when the opponent defected last round and otherwise cooperates based on score/defection counts. The trace simulates this parent against TFT-like opponents and against always-C, then adds a stateless test/exploit mode: while the opponent has never defected, defect on scheduled rounds (10,15,20,25,30) and then always defect; once the opponent defects, switch to the parent's conditional logic.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's check slot 10's fitness: 273.7. Our strategy with exploit might do better by getting more against always C (slots 6 and 9)."
STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional retaliator with immediate defection after opponent D, score-based defection, and probabilistic defection when opponent defects more than half the time. The trace simulates the parent against slot 0 and other population members, then adds an always-C exploit with scheduled test defections and a 20% forgiveness rule in conditional mode.
